description: ABOUT THE ROLE Rootstock Capital is building a BTC capital markets business, and we're hiring a small, senior team of two to three people to shape, grow and deliver it. Its first product is an institutional-grade, BTC-denominated investment fund that lets institutional and private Bitcoin holders earn yield and manage credit risk through a mixed portfolio of strategies, bridging traditional institutional demand and Bitcoin-native yield. As Director of Risk Management , you'll build and lead Rootstock Capital's risk function. You'll own the risk framework across market, credit, counterparty, liquidity, operational and protocol risk, spanning BTC, digital assets and traditional finance, and covering OTC, bilateral and exchange-traded activity. You'll be a founding member of the team, working alongside the VP Fund Management. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Risk framework and governance Design and own Rootstock Capital's risk framework: risk appetite; exposure, concentration and leverage limits; liquidity buckets; collateral haircuts; margin and drawdown triggers; and escalation procedures. Take risk policies and limits through board approval, and report regularly to the board and investment committee. Give independent risk sign-off on new strategies, products, venues and counterparties before launch. Risk modelling and analysis Build the models and analytics that measure market, credit, counterparty, liquidity and protocol risk across traditional and digital positions, including VaR, scenario analysis and stress testing. Stress-test the portfolio against BTC price shocks, liquidity crises, venue or counterparty failure, depeg events, protocol exploits and liquidation cascades. Model and evaluate complex transactions (secured lending, repo, basis and derivatives, structured products) and assess how risks interact and compound across on-chain and off-chain components. Monitor positions and exposures daily, and flag early when outcomes drift from limits or assumptions. Counterparty and credit risk Lead counterparty, venue and protocol due diligence: creditworthiness, custody arrangements, and smart-contract, bridge, oracle and governance risk. Set and monitor counterparty limits, collateral eligibility and margin terms. Legal and transaction documentation Review and negotiate the risk terms in fund, OTC and bilateral documents (ISDA/CSA, lending and repo agreements, collateral and margin terms, termination events and close-out provisions) with the Fund Asset Manager and legal counsel. Operational risk, controls and compliance Design operational risk controls across the trade lifecycle, settlement, reconciliation, custody and treasury that scale with both traditional and digital asset activity. Shape the processes that connect risk, execution and finance across digital and traditional OTC, bilateral and exchange-traded transactions. Work with compliance, legal, the fund administrator and auditors on regulatory obligations, audits and reporting. Product delivery Work with the Fund Asset Manager and commercial, technology, legal and compliance teams to take new products from idea to launch, making sure they are investable and structurally sound. WHAT YOU BRING Postgraduate degree in Finance, Computer Science or Mathematical Finance, plus a professional qualification in finance or risk (CFA, FRM, PRM or equivalent). 10+ years in risk management at asset managers, funds, banks, trading firms or digital asset businesses, including several years leading a risk function. Deep capital, asset and risk management experience across BTC, digital assets and traditional finance, including DeFi protocol risk. Strong financial modelling and risk analysis skills (stress testing, scenario analysis, VaR) across traditional and digital instruments, with hands-on Python, R or SQL. Hands-on experience designing operational risk controls across the trade lifecycle, custody and treasury for OTC, bilateral and exchange-traded activity. Experience reviewing and negotiating risk terms in fund, OTC and bilateral documents, and working within fund regulatory and compliance requirements. Proven leadership of high-performing teams, and the ability to explain complex risk clearly to boards, investors and regulators. ROOTIES BENEFITS At RootstockLabs , we don’t just offer a job, we offer a community. Here’s what you can expect when you join us: Competitive compensation package and unique benefits designed to support your growth and well-being. 100% Remote Work from Europe & Latin America, with access to global CoWorking spaces. Work-Life Balance: Paid vacation and sick leave days Continuous Learning: Access to training programs, language courses, and learning sponsorship annually. Unique Projects: Work with cutting-edge blockchain technology in a global, diverse team. ABOUT ROOTSTOCKLABS RootstockLabs is a key contributor to Rootstock, Bitcoin's Financial Infrastructure for lending, yield, and onchain capital markets. We build and commercialize the institutional infrastructure that turns Bitcoin into productive capital. What we do: Develop and commercialize Bitcoin-backed lending, tokenized real-world assets, and onchain financial strategies Who we work with: Leading custodians, asset managers, and financial institutions Why it matters: Rootstock is secured by 80%+ of Bitcoin's hash power and has run with 100% uptime since 2018 (bringing Ethereum-style programmability to the world's hardest money). Proof it works: 200+ dApps live on Rootstock, from BTCFi protocols like Sushiswap and Oku to institutional names like Mercado Bitcoin, Animoca Brands, and Paystand Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Event Design Coordinator (Remote / Europe)
description: Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction. Innovate with Tether Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the world’s most trusted stablecoin, USDT , relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services. But that’s just the beginning: Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities. Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET , our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing. Tether Education : Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity. Tether Evolution : At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways. Why Join Us? Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry. If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you. Are you ready to be part of the future? About the job We are seeking an Event Design Coordinator to manage the intake, production, and quality assurance of event-related creative requests coming from a wide range of teams across the business. This is a builder-and-gatekeeper role: you'll work hand-in-hand with designers to turn varied, often fast-turnaround requests into flawless deliverables, including booth graphics, signage, decks, digital assets, swag, and invites, while proactively spotting risks (timeline, brand, print spec, or logistical) before they become problems. We are not looking for someone who simply routes tickets. We're looking for someone who understands both the creative process and the operational realities of live events well enough to catch a misaligned bleed line, a missing dieline, or a vendor deadline that's about to slip, and to fix it before anyone else notices. Responsibilities Request Intake & Triage Serve as the primary point of contact for event-related creative requests coming from varied teams across Tether. Scope each request clearly: deliverable type, format (print vs. digital), quantity, deadline, dimension, venue/vendor constraints, and brand requirements. Flag conflicting timelines, unrealistic turnarounds, or missing information immediately, and propose a workable plan rather than waiting to be asked. Design Collaboration & Project Management Brief designers with complete, unambiguous specs so work is right the first time. Manage multiple concurrent event workstreams across different teams and deadlines without dropping details. Track status across all active requests and proactively surface bottlenecks before they affect the event date. Quality Assurance (Print & Digital) Review every designer deliverable before it goes back to the requesting team, checking brand consistency, copy accuracy, resolution, color mode (CMYK vs. RGB), bleed/trim/safe zones, file formats, and platform specs (e.g., booth panel dimensions, social crop ratios, slide aspect ratios). Catch errors that would be costly or embarrassing to fix on-site or post-launch (typos, wrong sizing, low-res exports, broken links, outdated logos). Maintain a QA checklist/process that scales across event types and gets sharper over time. Event Documentation & Knowledge Management Document and file all assets, briefs, and final deliverables for each event in a shared drive, using a clear, consistent structure. Organize files so the wider team can easily find past work, reuse assets, and cross-reference specs, timelines, or creative direction from previous events. Keep a running record of vendor details, production specs, and lessons learned per event to speed up planning for future ones. Risk & Logistics Ownership Anticipate what can go wrong, such as vendor lead times, print production windows, last-minute scope changes, and shipping delays, and build buffer and contingency plans into every project timeline. Coordinate with vendors and print/production partners as needed to confirm specs and delivery windows. Keep stakeholders across requesting teams and design aligned with clear, proactive status updates rather than reactive fire drills. Cross-Team Partnership Act as a trusted liaison between business requesters and the design team, protecting designers' time from ambiguous briefs while protecting requesters from missed deadlines. Continuously improve the intake and review process based on what goes wrong (or almost goes wrong) on each event. Requirements 5+ years of experience in event marketing, event production, creative operations, or project management with a strong events component. Proven experience managing print and digital production processes; you know what a dieline is, what "safe area" means, and why RGB assets can't go straight to print. Strong organizational and multitasking skills: demonstrated ability to manage several concurrent, cross-functional requests with competing deadlines. Sharp attention to detail, comfortable being the last line of defense before a deliverable ships. Experience reviewing and giving actionable feedback on creative work from designers, without needing to be a designer yourself. A proactive, risk-first mindset: you naturally ask "what could go wrong here?" and build a plan around the answer. Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable managing stakeholders across different teams with different priorities. Familiarity with project management tools (Asana, Monday, or similar) and design review tools like Figma Experience setting up shared drive structures or asset libraries for teams. Fluent in English and Spanish / Italian is a plus. Important information for candidates Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles: Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website. Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms. Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @ or @ We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately. When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website. Highlights Originally posted on Himalayas

Strong expertise in SystemVerilog, UVM (Universal Verification Methodology), assertion-based verification, and coverage-driven verification for complex hardware architectures. Strong collaborative mindset and problem-solving skills to work effectively with cross-functional FE Design, System, and SW teams. Fluency in English with excellent written and verbal communication skills. Highlights Leading and mentoring engineering teams, managing projects from concept to silicon qualification, and collaborating with key industry partners to deliver innovative memory solutions. description: ⌘Role Overview The Growth Product Manager at Timeleft owns the acquisition-to-purchase funnel: everything a new user encounters between first landing screen (on mobile app or mobile web) and a paid, booked seat. Timeleft connects strangers in real life — thousands of people every week, in more than 60 countries, around 10,000 bookings a day across different experiences from Dinners to Coffee and Drinks and more. Timeleft is a mobile-first subscription business: growth depends on flows that converts intent into a booked seat, and on a subscription that users continue to renew. This role owns onboarding and activation, paywall strategy, pricing and packaging across 3 platforms (iOS, Android, Web), and the experimentation programme that drives all of them. The role works closely with Marketing, Data and Engineering. It is accountable for revenue from new subscribers, and for the two components that determine it: conversion to purchase and lifetime value per subscriber. You will report to the VP of Product. ⌘Key Responsibilities 1. Conversion to Purchase Own conversion to purchase and lifetime value per subscriber across the full path from first screen to completed payment. Neither is a target on its own — improving one at the expense of the other is not a gain; total revenue from new subscribers is the measure. Map that path end to end across mobile app and mobile web, identify where intent is lost, and prioritise fixes by revenue impact. Own continuity between web and app: the handover from a web landing or checkout into the application, and the differences in payment, billing and refund behaviour between store and web purchase. Account for acquisition channel in funnel design: paid, organic and referral users arrive with different intent and require different flows. 2. Onboarding & Activation Own the onboarding flow: what is asked of new users, in what order, and how the answers are used. Define activation for Timeleft , instrument it, and maintain it as the company-wide definition. Reduce time and friction to the first booked seat while preserving the information that matching requires. 3. Paywalls, Pricing & Packaging Own paywall strategy: placement, timing, design and what is gated. Own pricing and packaging across markets and currencies, including trials, offers, upsells and win-back, and own ARPU as a result. Balance first-purchase conversion against renewal quality and attendance. 4. Experimentation Run a continuous experimentation programme across onboarding, paywalls and pricing. Apply consistent statistical standards: pre-registered hypotheses, adequate power, and decision criteria set before launch. Evaluate every experiment against downstream behaviour — attendance, renewal and LTV — in addition to its primary metric. 5. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Marketing on channel mix, creative strategy and continuity between advertising and the first in-app/landing screen. Partner with Data on instrumentation, attribution and experiment design. Coordinate the handover of activated users into the wider product experience, and define with the Core team what onboarding must collect. ⌘Expected Outcomes Revenue from new subscribers grows. Pricing and paywall changes are evaluated on total revenue, not on conversion rate alone. Conversion to purchase and activation are instrumented, trusted metrics that improve quarter over quarter. Onboarding is differentiated by acquisition channel and user intent rather than uniform. Paywall and pricing decisions are based on measured elasticity. Lifetime value per subscriber is held or improved as acquisition volume grows, without degradation in renewal quality or attendance. Experiment throughput is high and every result is readable against downstream retention. ⌘Skills & Competencies (Must Have & Nice to have) B2C mobile product depth: has owned a consumer mobile application where the application is the primary business surface, with practical knowledge of how iOS and Android and Mobile Web differ. Subscription monetization: experienced in paywalls, trials, pricing elasticity, tiering, upsells and win-back, and in the distinction between acquiring a subscriber and retaining one. Subscription economics: reads conversion and lifetime value together, distinguishes a conversion gain from a revenue gain, and recognises when a pricing change has increased volume at the expense of value. Funnel analytics: builds behavioural funnels and growth models, works directly with behavioural and payment data, and identifies conversion blockers from evidence. Experimentation rigour: sustains high experiment velocity alongside disciplined interpretation, including discontinuing tests that improve first purchase at the expense of retention. Conversion craft: understands the mechanics of a first purchase — framing, social proof, personalisation and timing — and applies them accurately. Cross-functional influence: operates effectively across Marketing, Data and Engineering without line authority; direct, structured, comfortable operating with founders and challenging decisions with evidence. ⌘ Required experience 5+ years in product management, growth or lifecycle roles, including direct ownership of a consumer subscription funnel. Demonstrable conversion-rate and revenue improvements in a consumer mobile product. Hands-on ownership of paywall and pricing experimentation. Proficient in analytics tooling and able to query data independently. Fluent English required Nice to have Marketplace or supply-constrained business experience. Experience with a product whose value is delivered offline. Experience operating across multiple markets and currencies. Originally posted on Himalayas

description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing. We are hiring multiple positions from early-career engineers to experienced architects focused on the different dimensions of dependable software: cybersecurity, quality, and safety. What does it take to bring the world’s open source software into mission-critical systems? At Canonical , we are driving the engineering discipline needed to build secure, reliable, and high-quality products that our automotive and industrial partners can depend on. Ubuntu is already the world’s most widely used Linux distribution in general; we want to make it the world’s best choice for the automotive and industrial sectors too. We operate at the boundary between upstream open source innovation and the industrial regulatory realities. Our engineers define the concepts, architectures, processes, verification strategies, and certification artifacts to transform a general-purpose platform into a dependable, certifiable foundation for automotive and industrial compute. This is systems-level engineering at scale, requiring precision, rigor, and a deep understanding of how complex software behaves in constrained, regulated environments. We are looking for engineers and architects who combine an open source hacker and builder mindset with respect for rigorous, standards-driven engineering. You will work across Canonical engineering teams and with leading industrial partners, helping to build this capability from the ground up and shaping how open source enters the most demanding technical domains. Location : This is a remote role based in the EMEA region. The role entails Translate automotive and industrial cybersecurity, quality and safety standards into actionable engineering requirements and perform gap analyses against current capabilities. Drive the creation of structured engineering artifacts, including requirements, traceability models, risk analysis, test strategies, and certification documentation. Collaborate with Canonical engineering teams to align development practices with industrial compliance needs. Design, implement, and execute verification and validation activities required to qualify Ubuntu and other components for regulated environments. Develop and improve automation and tooling to scale traceability, testing, compliance evidence generation, and reporting. Engage with industrial partners to understand their expectations, align external expectations and internal capabilities, and support audits and technical reviews. Contribute to the continuous improvement of Canonical ’s internal processes and standards capability as the team scales. What we are looking for in you Strong software engineering foundation with experience in developing complex systems on Linux. Professional experience with C, C++, and Python in production environments. Demonstrated experience working within automotive, industrial, or other regulated environments governed by safety, cybersecurity, or quality standards (such as ISO 26262, ISO/SAE 21434, IEC 61508, IEC 62443, SOTIF, or (A)SPICE), and applying them in practice. Experience in system or software architecture, implementation, or verification and validation of complex embedded systems. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce precise technical documentation. Ability to collaborate effectively in a distributed team and engage with industrial partners. Additional experience that is valuable Contributions to open source projects, particularly in the area of Software Defined Vehicles. Knowledge of Debian packaging. Experience with Rust or safety-critical software development. What we offer colleagues We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical is an equal-opportunity employer We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products.Whatever your identity we will give your application fair consideration . title: Senior Product Security Engineer (all genders)
description: Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travellers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers including Google Maps and Booking.com. We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading venture capital investors including TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum, and Northzone, and are headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond. We are looking for our first dedicated Senior Product/Application Security Engineer to build our AppSec practice from the ground up. This is a greenfield opportunity with a real attack surface: public partner-facing APIs and payment flows. You will own secure development, define what gets reviewed, implement security gates, build the "paved road" for ~150 engineers, and see the impact of your work in production within weeks. What you will do: Lead threat modeling and secure design reviews for high-risk changes, partner integrations, and payment flows. Implement, tune, and enforce security gates in GitLab CI/CD (SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, and DAST) while minimizing developer friction. Act as the primary technical owner for triaging, reproducing, and prioritizing findings from bug bounties, partner pentests, and automated scanners. Work hands-on with the DevOps team to implement GCP organizational policies, IAM least-privilege architectures, and Cloud Armor (WAF/rate limiting). Establish a security-champions network across engineering squads and leverage automation/AI-assisted tooling to scale code reviews effectively. Own vulnerability management end to end: a risk-ranked backlog, remediation SLAs, an escalation path, and closing findings together with the teams. Scope and coordinate the annual external penetration test and produce secure-development evidence for PCI-DSS and ISO 27001. Workplace: We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe and a HQ in Berlin. Requirements Who you are: You bring 5+ years in Product/Application Security (or 3+ years plus a strong software engineering/web-pentesting background), with a track record of true ownership. You read and write production code (Python, Go, TypeScript, Ruby, etc.) and deeply understand web frameworks, CI/CD, and Kubernetes. You have deep knowledge of web and API security, specifically authentication/authorization models (OAuth2, JWT), rate limiting, tenant isolation, IDOR, and XSS. You have strong cloud security fundamentals (GCP preferred), specifically regarding public exposure, secrets hygiene, and WAF rules. You have run threat modelling and secure design reviews on real systems (STRIDE or similar). Hands-on with SAST/SCA/secrets scanning in CI (Aikido, Semgrep, Snyk or similar). You prioritize by real-world risk, propose trade-offs rather than demanding perfection, and communicate complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership. Bonus Points: You have experience securing high-volume, multi-tenant B2B APIs and utilizing AI tooling to accelerate triage and review. What you can expect: You will join a fast-paced travel tech company with a flat organizational structure. You will have exciting opportunities, ownership, and responsibility and contribute directly to the success of the company. You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day! We have a flexible work policy with the option of working remotely and international opportunities arising as we continue to expand our global footprint – Our heart is in Berlin, but you’ll find us across the globe. You will get a competitive salary. Our hiring team for this role: Your Talent Partner (TP) and point of contact is Lorena Rebenciuc, and the Hiring Manager (HM) is Ilya Isakov. For any queries, contact your Talent Partner at . Do you want to work on a product that is used by millions of people daily with a high load, availability and scalability, and most advanced technology? Come join us! Originally posted on Himalayas

description: über juni JUNI ist ein gemeinnütziges Ökosystem für Wissenschaft und Ausgründungen in Berlin. Wir betreiben unsere Programme über sieben SaaS-Tools hinweg — Newsletter, Events, Community, CRM, Formulare, Bewerbungen, Coworking — und darunter eine Postgres-Datenbank, die der eine Ort sein soll, an dem eine Person existiert. Auf die Datenbank kommt es an. Ein aufgelöster Datensatz pro Person und pro Organisation, eine append-only-Zeile pro Interaktion, und ein deterministischer Weg zu entscheiden, zu welcher Person ein eingehender Payload gehört. Ziel ist, den Weg vom ersten Kontaktpunkt bis zum Meilenstein messbar zu machen. Die Verbindungsschicht zwischen den Tools und dieser Datenbank ist die Aufgabe. deine aufgaben Die Schicht bauen, die unsere Systeme mit einer Datenbank verbindet — in beide Richtungen — und uns dabei helfen, das Datenmodell richtig hinzubekommen. Die Form der Daten steht weitgehend, und jedes neue System stellt sie auf die Probe. Quellen sind sich nicht einig, was als eine Person zählt, wann etwas passiert ist, und ob sie es zweimal melden. Das zu klären — und zu erkennen, wann das Modell angepasst werden muss, statt es um eine Quelle herumzubiegen — ist der Kern der Arbeit. Wir suchen jemanden, der das mit uns durchdenkt und für einen bestimmten Entwurf argumentiert, nicht nur umsetzt, was spezifiziert ist. dein profil Umfang Inbound Jedes System in die Datenbank. Mehrere Pipelines pro System — Quellen melden sehr unterschiedliche Dinge. Identitätsauflösung über Systeme hinweg. Outbound Manche Zustände entstehen bei uns, nicht im Tool. Die Datenbank entscheidet und schiebt an die Plattform, die es ausführt. Beide Richtungen sauber halten Plattformen melden zurück und widersprechen uns manchmal. Wer sich abgemeldet hat, darf nicht wieder hinzugefügt werden. Reporting KPI-Daten müssen in einem BI-Tool ankommen. Sie dorthin zu bringen gehört dazu, Dashboards bauen nicht. Suche Den Datenbestand in natürlicher Sprache durchsuchbar machen. Dokumentation Entscheidungen schriftlich, Pipelines in GitHub. Nicht Teil der Rolle Frontend. Es gibt keins und es ist keins geplant. Voraussetzungen Integration gegen Third-Party-APIs und Webhooks , in der Tiefe: Pagination, Retries, Signaturprüfung, Rate Limits, undokumentierte Payload-Strukturen, verspätete und vertauschte Events, Quellen, die bei jeder Änderung feuern und nicht sagen, was sich geändert hat. Bidirektionale Synchronisation zwischen Systemen, die beide dasselbe Feld für ihres halten — Loop-Vermeidung, Echo-Unterdrückung, eine klare Antwort darauf, wer bei Konflikten gewinnt. Postgres als Anwendungsdatenbank, nicht nur als Ziel. plpgsql-Funktionen, Trigger, Constraints und RLS, um Regeln beim Schreiben durchzusetzen. Wenn sich deine SQL-Erfahrung auf Transformationen nach dem Load beschränkt, passt die Rolle nicht. Idempotenz als Gewohnheit, nicht als Nachgedanke. Eine Pipeline, die erneut läuft und nichts verändert, ist der Abnahmetest. Sauberes Arbeiten mit Git — Migrationen, PRs, Review. Arbeit mit personenbezogenen Daten unter der DSGVO, und ein Verständnis dafür, warum das einschränkt, was überhaupt eingelesen wird. Englisch in Schrift. Die Arbeit läuft überwiegend asynchron, und was du baust, muss für jemanden lesbar sein, der nicht dabei war. Hilfreich, nicht erforderlich n8n oder ein anderer Orchestrator · Supabase · Relevanzarbeit an einem Suchindex — Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Meilisearch oder vergleichbar; Cluster-Betrieb ist nicht der Teil, den wir brauchen · Erfahrung als einzige Person auf einem System · Deutsch. wir bieten Zusammenarbeit Remote und überwiegend asynchron, aber nicht wortlos — gerade am Anfang sind echte Gespräche eingeplant, während du dich in die Systeme und ihre Zusammenhänge einarbeitest. Rahmen Freiberuflich, Start so bald wie möglich. Zunächst drei Monate; danach sehen wir, was gebraucht wird. Berlin oder Remote innerhalb der EU. Originally posted on Himalayas

If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply. About the Role: We are seeking an Analytics Engineer to own and execute the vision for our data transformation layer. You will be at the heart of our data platform, which processes hundreds of millions of events daily from a wide array of sources, including transactional databases, API logs, CRMs, payment systems, and marketing platforms. You will join our 100% remote team and work closely with Data Engineers (who manage data ingestion) and Data Scientists and Business Users (who consume your data models). Your primary responsibility will be to use dbt and Trino on our GCP-based, open-source data infrastructure to build robust, scalable data models. These models are critical for stakeholders across the company—from finance and operations to the executive team—and are delivered via BI tools, reports, and reverse ETL systems. What You'll Do: Own the Transformation Layer: Design, build, and maintain scalable data models using dbt and SQL to support diverse business needs, from monthly financial reporting to near-real-time operational metrics. Set Technical Standards: Establish and enforce best practices for data modelling, development, testing, and monitoring to ensure data quality, integrity (up to cent-level precision), and discoverability. Enable Stakeholders: Collaborate directly with finance, operations, customer success, and marketing teams to understand their requirements and deliver reliable data products. Integrate and Deliver: Create repeatable patterns for integrating our data models with BI tools and reverse ETL processes, enabling consistent metric reporting across the business. Ensure Quality: Champion high standards for development, including robust change management, source control, code reviews, and data monitoring as our products and data evolve. What You Need (Must-Haves): 4+ years of experience in analytics engineering or data engineering with a strong focus on the "T" (transformation) in ELT. Proven track record of owning data products end-to-end, applying analytics and data engineering best practices to ensure data quality, scalability, and robust data models. Comfortable working with ambiguity and collaborating with stakeholders to define requirements; able to take ownership with minimal oversight in a fast-paced environment. Experience proactively identifying and implementing improvements to data warehouse performance and ETL efficiency. Technical Versatility: Expert-level SQL and DBT skills for complex queries and data transformations. Proficiency in Python for transformations that extend beyond SQL. Hands-on experience with query optimization across OLTP and OLAP systems (e.g., Postgres, Iceberg). Proficiency with Semantic Layer modelling (e.g. Cube, dbt Semantic Layer). Experience owning CI/CD workflows and establishing team-wide standards for version control and code review (e.g., Git). Familiarity with cloud environments (GCP or AWS). Nice to Haves: Experience with data ingestion tools (e.g., Airbyte) and orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow). Domain experience for brokerage operations or a passion for financial markets and modelling financial datasets. title: [REMOTE] Senior LiveOps Developer - Mobile Games
description: Senior LiveOps Developer - Mobile Games Remote - Full Time CrazyGames , one of the world's largest browser game platforms with over 60 million monthly active users, is doubling down on its IP portfolio. We own the games we publish, and we treat each one as a live product rather than a finished project. We're looking for a Senior LiveOps Developer who has already done this on mobile. Someone who has taken a title through soft launch and global launch, knows which live systems need to exist before you scale UA behind a game, and can build them. This is a hands-on development role. You'll write the code for the events, the progression systems, the offers, the economy and the remote config that keep a game growing. You'll also be the person who looks at a game's numbers and says what should ship next and why, because you've run this playbook before at a mobile publisher. What this role is not: greenfield game development, or working through a feature backlog someone else wrote. You'll be inside existing codebases almost all of the time, on games that already have players, and you'll be the one deciding what those games need. Key outcomes for the role Within 1 month , you've onboarded to one of our live published titles, gotten comfortable in its codebase, shipped your first live update to production on web and mobile, and given us your first read on what that game's LiveOps setup is missing. Within 3 months , you own the LiveOps roadmap for at least one title. You've set an update cadence, shipped a meaningful live system (event framework, progression, offers, remote config, economy tuning), and we can see the effect in retention or monetization. Within 6 months , you've taken a title through the run-up to global launch. The live systems, the event calendar, the balancing and the tooling are in place before UA scales behind it, and you decided what belonged there. Within 12 months , LiveOps is a repeatable system across our IP portfolio rather than something that depends on you personally. Multiple live titles run in parallel on the cadence, tooling and playbook you put in place. On a typical day you might Look at retention, session length, ARPDAU and conversion for a live title, and decide what to build next. Ship a seasonal event, content drop or offer to one of our live IP games on web and mobile. Build the live system behind it: event framework, remote config, A/B test, progression or economy change. Dive into an unfamiliar codebase to plan how a new system slots in without breaking what's already there. Tell us a game is not ready for global launch yet, and what has to exist first. Design and implement a new game mode, progression system or monetization hook tailored to the genre. Align with the Publishing team on the LiveOps roadmap and prioritization across titles. Maintain clean Git history, write down what you did, and make sure the next update is easier than the last. What we offer Join a rapidly growing publishing team at a company with 50M+ monthly users and proven platform reach. Make a real impact by directly shaping the games millions of people actually play, week after week. A lot of responsibility and freedom. We hire only experts and trust them to deliver excellent results. Flexible working hours and location. The results are what counts! 1 to 2 team weeks per year. We pay for flights and accommodation so you can have fun with the team. The opportunity to play games and claim it's work. Requirements You're a great fit if you Have 2+ years running LiveOps on shipped mobile titles. Update cadence, events, progression, economy, offers, and the reasoning behind each of them. This is the requirement we weigh most heavily. If your experience is game development without live ownership, this is not the role. Have been through a mobile soft launch and a global launch , and know what has to be in place before UA scales behind a game. Bring a playbook, not just execution. You've seen how strong mobile publishers run live titles, and you can apply that here instead of waiting for someone to hand you a backlog. Have 3+ years of professional game development experience with shipped titles, and are still hands-on. You build the live systems yourself rather than specifying them for someone else. Read metrics as a developer, not just as a consumer of dashboards. Retention, session length, ARPDAU, conversion and cohort behaviour drive what you build next. Have strong mobile game development experience (iOS and Android), and understand the differences in performance, input and UX across platforms. Work with analytics, A/B testing, remote config and live tooling as part of your normal workflow, not as something a separate team owns. Are comfortable with monetization and ads SDKs in a LiveOps context (events, offers, balancing). Are fluent in multiple languages and ecosystems, at minimum C# and JavaScript/TypeScript, and have a solid grasp of software architecture and OOP principles. Can step into an existing codebase, read it, understand it, and extend it confidently. Use Git effectively in team environments and care about leaving the codebase better than you found it. Are pragmatic, detail-oriented, and focused on getting high-quality updates shipped fast. Are a strong team player with a true ownership mindset: you collaborate openly, take full responsibility for what you ship, and treat every game you work on as your own product to nurture and grow. Are proficient in English (working language). Nice to have Web game development experience. Our platform is browser-first, so our games ship on web as well as mobile. We'd rather hire the right live experience and get you up to speed on web than compromise on the LiveOps side. Multiplayer and networking experience: client/server architecture, real-time sync, matchmaking, dedicated servers. Open to learning if you haven't done it yet, but excited about it. Game design instincts: the ability to look at one of our games and have informed opinions on what to build next, how to fit a feature to a specific genre or audience, and how to keep the experience cohesive as it grows. Ability to speak Turkish (mother tongue of most members of the Publishing team). Highlights As part of our Publishing team, you'll take ownership of the games we own. You'll push regular updates, ship new content and features, and run live events. Originally posted on Himalayas

description: Credit Decision Scientist CRNCY · Senior · Remote · USD contractor Why this work matters Across the developing world, access to credit still depends on paperwork most people can't produce. A teacher six years in the same job. A vendor who has run the same stall for a decade. Creditworthy, both — and illegible to a system built for someone else. CRNCY exists to close that gap, using technology to open doors for the people who need them most. Every rule you write here decides who gets through. Mission Help CRNCY become the world's best underwriter of credit risk using unstructured and alternative data. We operate in markets where customers often have limited traditional credit information. Our objective is to make better lending decisions under uncertainty and continuously improve risk-adjusted profitability. What You'll Do •Analyze portfolio performance and identify opportunities to improve profitability through credit strategy. •Model the probability of repayment, default and fraud from incomplete and alternative data, and build the statistical inference behind it. •Turn that analysis into the credit rules themselves: approval strategy, underwriting requirements, first-loan sizing and customer segmentation. •Optimize underwriting requirements and reduce unnecessary customer friction. •Design and assess experiments to improve lending outcomes. •Quantify trade-offs between growth, risk, customer experience and profitability. •Translate analysis into practical underwriting and portfolio recommendations. You do this work yourself. There is no analytics team to delegate to. You frame the question, build the analysis, and own the decision that comes out of it. What We're Looking For Experience in at least one of: portfolio strategy or analytics, underwriting strategy, lending strategy, risk management, or another analytical role involving high-consequence decision-making under uncertainty. Experience in consumer lending or credit is not required. We are far more interested in exceptional decision-makers than in experience in any particular industry. We are interested in candidates who have: •Used data and probabilistic reasoning to make or influence important business decisions. •Evaluated trade-offs between competing objectives under uncertainty. •Applied analytical judgment rather than relying solely on predefined rules or models. •Translated analysis into practical business decisions and recommendations. • Been accountable for the business outcomes of those decisions, not simply the quality of the analysis. Working capability, hands-on: statistical inference and probability; causal reasoning and selection bias; practical modeling — logistic regression, scorecards, gradient boosting — with clean validation discipline and no data leakage; experiment design and power; expected-value analysis; segmentation. Python and SQL at analysis-and-modeling level. You write your own code. Required Academic Background A degree from a strong university in a quantitative discipline: Decision Science, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, or Computer Science with significant quantitative coursework. Your training should have covered probability and statistics, decision-making under uncertainty, optimization, mathematical modeling, econometrics, operations research or risk analysis. Above all, we are looking for someone who naturally thinks probabilistically — comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, weighing uncertainty, and updating their judgment as new evidence becomes available. Language: fluent English and Spanish. Both required. What This Role Is Not This is not: •A Machine Learning Engineer role •A Data Engineering role •An AI Infrastructure role •A Machine Learning Research role • A traditional Data Scientist role focused primarily on model development Candidates whose experience is primarily centered on building models, pipelines, platforms or technical infrastructure will not be considered. What we are screening out is the candidate whose output is a model. Here, the output is a decision — you simply have to build the analysis yourself to get there. How We Work • Honest and direct. Feedback here is unvarnished and immediate. You'll get it, and we expect it back. • Unafraid to fail. Most of what you test won't work. We would rather run the experiment and find out than defend a rule nobody has questioned. • Committed to excellence. High standards, applied to ourselves before anyone else. • Dedicated to the customer. The person on the other side of the decision is the reason the work matters. The Setup • USD contractor. Fully remote, location-flexible, with meaningful daily overlap with the Americas. •You'll work directly with our credit and finance leadership and with the founder. Short path from analysis to decision. •Real ownership from day one, across multiple markets. Originally posted on Himalayas

Self-driven and collaborative, with a track record of contributing to high-impact research projects. Bachelor’s degree or higher in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, or a related field. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with the development or evaluation of rubrics, especially for AI and data annotation workflows. Familiarity with designing datasets or protocols for AI training and human review processes. Previous collaboration with interdisciplinary or remote teams on data-driven biology projects. title: Curation & Funding Coordinator
description: Job Vision Trust is the funding and development arm of the larger family of brands. Trust exists to provide filmmakers with capital and resources to bring their visions to life. Through direct film funding to commissioning work that generates revenue to buyouts of previous work to secure capital for a future project, Trust works with filmmakers in many ways to allow them to create on their own terms. Trust then takes that footage and licenses it to generate its own revenue which allows us to fund more projects. This role includes management of the contract editors who shape and curate footage, sourcing and buying pre-made assets, and maintaining the administrative work that this work requires. You'll report and collaborate closely with the Director of Trust to learn and grow the business but primarily invest your time and effort in editor direction, curation, and buyout pipeline. What You’ll Do Editor management and footage curation Manage a roster of contract editors, including finding new editors, assigning work, setting curation standards, reviewing output, and giving clear feedback Own curation quality across footage: what makes the cut, how it's organized, and how it's prepped for the library Keep editors unblocked and on schedule, balancing efficiency with quality Maintain and refine curation guidelines as the catalog and Trust's needs evolve Asset buyouts Source pre-made assets that fit Trust's library strategy and gaps Evaluate assets for quality, rights, fit, and ROI before purchase Negotiate and execute buyouts, tracking spend against budget Maintain clean records of what was bought, from whom, and under what terms Help analyze and evaluate buyout process to ensure that each opportunity is fair and valuable Administrative Own the paperwork and tracking tied to editor contracts and asset purchases (agreements, invoices, payment coordination, rights documentation, talent and property releases) Own the management of footage as it moves through the pipeline (footage review, tagging, featuring stand out footage, and operating within Trust’s footage management platform) Keep acquisition and curation data accurate and current in our systems Report on pipeline status, spend, and throughput to Director of Trust Coordinate across Trust and the wider FM org as needed Requirements What We’re Looking For Experience managing contractors or freelancers, ideally editors or creative talent A strong eye for footage quality and a sense for what makes a library valuable - understanding what’s trending in advertising Comfort with buyout/licensing negotiating and the rights questions that come with them Organized and detail-driven Self-directed and able to own a workflow end-to-end Clear, direct communicator Nice To Have Background in commercial producing, post-production, or media licensing Familiarity with digital asset managers and project management platforms like ClickUp Experience tracking budgets or spend Experience negotiating deals for projects What Success Looks Like Library curation stays top tier, with footage selected, organized, and prepped to a consistently high standard Contract editors operate with clear direction, accountability, and strong, on-time output Asset buyouts are well-sourced, fairly priced, and aligned to library strategy and gaps Buyout spend stays on budget and delivers strong value per dollar Rights, contracts, and acquisition records remain clean, accurate, and audit-ready Curation standards stay current as the catalog and Trust's needs evolve The curation and buyout pipeline aligns smoothly with commissioned and funded production work Workflows align effectively with broader FM systems, processes, and priorities Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Senior DevOps Engineer (m/w/d)
description: was bieten wir? Bei DACHS IT sollst du nicht einfach nur „eine Stelle“ haben, sondern ein Arbeitsumfeld, das zu deinem Leben, deinen Stärken und deinen Zielen passt. Deshalb bieten wir dir: Remote-First als gelebtes Modell Wir arbeiten seit Jahren konsequent remote. Du entscheidest, von wo du am produktivsten bist – Homeoffice, Shared Office oder eine Mischung aus beidem. Flexible Arbeitszeiten mit Eigenverantwortung Du kannst dir deine Arbeit im Rahmen der Projekte zeitlich flexibel über die Woche einteilen. Uns sind Verlässlichkeit im Team und transparente Kommunikation wichtiger als Präsenz am Schreibtisch. Spannende Projekte statt Routine-Tickets Gemeinsam finden wir Projekte, die zu deinem Profil und deiner Entwicklung passen – z. B. Plattformaufbau, Cloud-Migration, Automatisierung, Operations oder technische Schulungen bei Kund:innen. Weiterbildung, Zertifizierungen & Wissensaustausch Regelmäßige Schulungen und Zertifizierungen sind fest eingeplant – mit Kostenübernahme und Freistellung. Dazu kommen interner Wissensaustausch, Sparrings auf Augenhöhe und Raum, dich fachlich wie methodisch weiterzuentwickeln. Moderne Ausstattung & Arbeitsumgebung Du erhältst moderne Hardware, die passende Software sowie das benötigte Equipment, damit du effizient und komfortabel arbeiten kannst. Attraktive Rahmenbedingungen Neben einem fairen Festgehalt bekommst du eine jährliche Beteiligung am Unternehmensgewinn. Je nach Rolle besteht zudem die Option auf einen Firmenwagen. Transparente Feedbackkultur & Entwicklung Wir setzen nicht auf jährliche Pflichttermine, sondern auf regelmäßige, ehrliche Gespräche auf Augenhöhe – du gibst uns Feedback, wir dir. So wissen wir alle, woran wir sind, und können unsere gemeinsamen nächsten Entwicklungsschritte gezielt unterstützen. Gesundheit, Freizeit & Sicherheit Du erhältst 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr, die nicht verfallen, sowie zusätzliche Absicherung, zum Beispiel durch eine Gruppen-Unfallversicherung. So bist du nicht nur beruflich, sondern auch privat gut aufgestellt. Teamkultur & gemeinsame Erlebnisse Trotz Remote-First ist uns persönlicher Austausch wichtig: Wir treffen uns regelmäßig zu gemeinsamen Aktivitäten – mal locker bei einem Get-together, mal zum gemeinsamen Workshop, mal aktiv bei Ausflügen – und sorgen so für echten Zusammenhalt abseits des Bildschirms. wen suchen wir? Als erfahrener Professional überzeugst du unsere Kunden durch ein souveränes Auftreten und fundiertes Wissen in Cloud- sowie Container-Technologien. Mit deinem empirisch-agilen Mindset entwickelst du passgenaue Lösungen und begleitest deren Umsetzung engagiert vor Ort oder remote. Dabei schätzen wir deine Eigeninitiative ebenso wie deine Teamfähigkeit und deine ausgeprägte Leidenschaft für die direkte Kundenberatung, bei Bedarf auch als Rufbereitschaft oder direkt vor Ort. was machst du bei uns? Als Senior DevOps Engineer betreust und berätst du unsere Kunden in allen technischen Fragen rund um die Themen Infrastruktur-Architektur, -Operations und -integration: Du trägst fundierte Empfehlungen zu Design- / Architektur-Entscheidungen bei. Du kümmerst dich um den Aufbau und die Integration von Plattformen, Pipelines und anderen Komponenten. Du erklärst Best Practices und vermittelst sie didaktisch. Du betreibst Fehlersuche/Debugging effizient und gibst die Erkenntnisse weiter. Du stellst Dokumentationen, Gits und andere Quellen zusammen, um tiefergehende Fragen zu beantworten. Du gibst technische Schulungen. Du berätst und vermittelst beim Umgang mit Drittanbietern / dem Herstellersupport. was bringst du mit? Technical Skills Must-have Kubernetes mindestens auf CKA/CKS-Level Alternativ OCP/OpenShift Kenntnisse mit Zertifizierung(en) oberhalb von EX180 Linux mit mindestens LPIC 1 (besser LPI-304/-305 oder gar „DevOps Tools Engineer“) alternativ RHCE Grundkenntnisse in Terraform und Ansible Projekterfahrungen mit und erweiterte Kenntnisse in mindestens einem der folgenden Cloud Stacks AWS GKE MS Azure OSP/Openstack Nice-to-have Contributer zur Kubernetes Entwicklung Erweiterte Terraform Kenntnisse Erweiterte Ansible Kenntnisse Kenntnisse der Go Language Soft Skills Must-have Deutsch und Englisch auf Business Level (C1/C2) in Wort und Schrift Berater-Mindset & -Skills Projekterfahrung im agilen Umfeld / mit Scrum Kanban-Kenntnisse Kommunikationsstark Moderations- und Deeskalationsmethoden Nice-to-have Scrum Master/PO Zertifizierung Lernmethodiken/Didaktik zur Schulungsdurchführung wie sieht der bewerbungsprozess bei uns aus? Wenn du dich bei uns bewirbst, begleiten wir dich transparent durch mehrere klar strukturierte Schritte. Uns ist wichtig, dass du jederzeit weißt, wo du stehst – deshalb erhältst du in jeder Phase zeitnah Rückmeldung und alle nötigen Infos zum weiteren Ablauf. In der Regel durchläufst du dabei folgende Schritte: Screening Wir sichten deine Unterlagen sorgfältig und bewerten, ob deine Erfahrungen, Kompetenzen und Ziele zu der ausgeschriebenen Rolle und zu DACHS IT passen – auf dieser Basis entscheiden wir über eine Einladung zum Kennenlernen. Kennenlerngespräch In einem 30–45-minütigen Videocall lernst du ein Mitglied unseres Teams kennen. Ihr sprecht über deinen Hintergrund, unsere Kultur, Erwartungen beider Seiten und habt Raum für Fragen. Technisches Interview In einem 60-minütigen Termin löst du gemeinsam mit ein bis zwei unserer Consultants anspruchsvolle technische Aufgaben. Dabei geht es uns darum, deine Herangehensweise, dein Fachwissen und deine Zusammenarbeit im Team kennenzulernen. Persönliches Gespräch Anschließend triffst du unseren Geschäftsführer Alexander. Ihr besprecht verbleibende Fragen, Rahmenbedingungen und wie eine gemeinsame Zukunft bei DACHS IT konkret aussehen könnte. Angebot Stimmt die Vorstellung auf beiden Seiten, erhältst du ein Angebot von uns – transparent, nachvollziehbar und mit allen wichtigen Details. Originally posted on Himalayas

title: 🌍 Civil / Structural Engineer, Remote- Contract
description: Role Title: Civil / Structural Engineer Role Type: Contract Location: Remote Required Skills: Revit ArchiCAD Civil Engineering Structural Engineering BIM tools In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. Scope of Work: Create, review, and refine detailed civil and structural drawing sets, including plans, elevations, sections, and schedules, using BIM tools such as Revit or ArchiCAD. Author and manage BIM models, ensuring accurate representation of complex or multi-building projects and full compliance with relevant code families (Eurocode, ACI, ASCE, IS, BS, etc.). Export and validate IFC files (IFC 2x3 or IFC4), confirming geometry, classification, and mapping integrity for design coordination and data interoperability. Document and communicate technical decisions and design rationale clearly through written and verbal channels, with a focus on clarity and precision. Contribute real-world insights by evaluating project requirements, identifying constructability issues, and suggesting improvements based on professional experience. Assess and provide feedback on the functionality and usability of BIM tools or data workflows. Deliver high-quality domain input that will directly inform the training and evaluation of AI-powered engineering solutions. Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or Architecture (Master’s degree preferred). Minimum of 5 years of hands-on, post-degree practice authoring complete drawing sets and leading model development, not limited to markups or reviews. At least 3 years of daily, expert-level BIM authoring experience in Revit, ArchiCAD, or BlenderBIM, including experience with IFC export and validation. Direct experience in projects requiring multidisciplinary coordination and delivery of complex or multi-building solutions. Demonstrated code literacy, with the ability to reference and apply Eurocode, ACI, ASCE, IS, or BS standards in design work. Fluency in written and spoken English, with a strong focus on precise articulation and clarity in technical communication. Nice to have: Professional licensing (PE, CEng, Chartered), experience with openBIM scripting (ifcopenshell, Python), knowledge of clash detection/model checking (Navisworks, Solibri), engineering analysis tools (ETABS, SAP2000, Robot, Tekla), custom BIM families, or prior data annotation for AI projects. description: Terms of Reference: Independent Consultancy - Technical Planning and Coordination for the Open Energy Research and Analytics Consortium (ORA) Background:The Open Energy Research and Analytics Consortium (ORA) is an open energy data partnership between the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), Ember, Global Energy Monitor (GEM), Open Energy Transition (OET), and TransitionZero. Through a shared governance structure and a Secretariat currently housed at GEM, the consortium is working to build an open energy intelligence system based on trusted data, open-source tools, and collaborative analysis. ORA’s members have already developed the expertise to build every component needed for a shared open data infrastructure as well as reproducible modeling, data pipelines, versioned and citable data, quality metadata, exploration tools, and aggregate data for validation. These components have not yet been coordinated in a cohesive system, and many of the ORA organizations have built similar supporting infrastructure separately. This leaves users and partners to repeatedly reconcile definitions, identifiers, formats, and methodologies, which limits interoperability, auditability, and reuse. The growing use of AI systems for energy questions adds urgency: the standardization, versioning, and source documentation needed to integrate data across ORA are also needed to make open, verified, citable data legible to AI systems. ORA is entering a 12-month foundational phase to turn the consortium’s vision into an agreed technical and governance blueprint for an open energy data platform and orchestration system, including its audiences, governance, shared standards, and technical architecture for integrating member datasets, open models, and analyses. ORA is committed to ensuring that its core datasets, shared infrastructure, and collaborative tools remain open-source and publicly available. Objective: ORA seeks an independent consultant, serving as Technical Coordinator, to facilitate and project manage the technical planning of building a shared data infrastructure across the five member organizations. The consultancy includes the interviews and research needed to develop concrete, detailed proposals for how members’ data can be integrated and supports members in agreeing on shared standards, a recommended architecture, and a roadmap for the next phase of the platform and the flagship product, the Open Energy Outlook. The result will be a consortium plan co-authored with the members. Scope of Work: The Consultant will provide facilitation, project management, and technical analysis for ORA’s defined 12-month foundational planning phase. The Consultant will carry out the following work: Facilitation and Consortium Engagement: Facilitate the planning process with all five ORA members, preparing agendas and materials, guiding discussions, building consensus among members with different practices and priorities, and documenting decisions and next steps. Interview the data leads at each member organization to assess data assets, systems, workflows, and priority user needs. Facilitate a shared definition of the platform’s priority users (for example, energy modelers, policy analysts, journalists, civil-society researchers, planners in developing geographies, and AI systems) and the access patterns, tools, and guarantees each needs. Lead members through review of, and decisions on, the proposed shared protocols, architecture options, and data hub scope, ensuring all members have meaningful input. Project Management: Develop and manage an integrated workplan for the foundational phase, with milestones, dependencies, and responsibilities across the five member organizations. Track progress, risks, decisions, and action items. Coordinate with the ORA Secretariat on communication with members and ORA leads. Coordinate with GEM on the data hub proof of concept. The Consultant will define its requirements with the members, and GEM will manage the build. Technical Planning and Analysis Develop a centralized map of the datasets, scrapers, and in-house data held across the five members, and identify gaps and opportunities for greater interoperability. Develop proposed common schemas, identifiers, and metadata documentation, including a framework for a jointly governed identifier crosswalk linking each organization’s records. Guide the members to develop shared approaches to automated validation and open, machine-readable documentation. Analyze and recommend a design for the data platform (whether hosted, federated, or hybrid, and potentially varying by data product), ensuring datasets are clearly versioned and provenance is traced to primary sources. Work with GEM’s Chief Data Officer to contribute to a strategy for presenting the consortium’s trusted datasets to AI systems as a preferred source for energy and climate queries, and a structured learning exchange on AI-assisted research methods. Scope and define requirements for a limited proof of concept showing how a centralized hub/platform could serve particular user groups, and assess the prototype, which will be built by data engineering contractors working under GEM’s direction. Co-author the consortium plan with the five members and prepare an implementation-ready technical and governance roadmap for the next phase. Deliverables The Consultant will produce the deliverables below. The inception workplan will set out agreed delivery dates, review responsibilities, and acceptance criteria for each deliverable. Changes to scope, deliverables, or milestones require mutual written agreement between GEM and the consultant, following consultation with the ORA Secretariat Inception report and integrated work plan Assessment report on members’ data assets, systems, and priority user needs Cross-member data map and gap analysis Agreed priority audiences and use cases Draft shared approaches to metadata, identifiers, validation, and data documentation Options paper on platform architecture Architecture recommendation and draft shared data protocols Requirements and scope for the data hub proof of concept, handed over to GEM Final consortium plan, including the roadmap for the next phase Meeting agendas and notes, and monthly progress reports Timing and Payment Structure The consultancy is expected to begin in mid-December and will run for 12 months from the agreed start date. Any extension will require a separate written agreement covering scope, duration, and fees subject to funding availability. The estimated level of effort is equivalent to approximately 20 hours per week over the assignment. This is a planning estimate rather than a requirement to work a fixed weekly schedule. The consultant will organize their time to meet agreed milestones and participate in mutually scheduled consortium meetings. The proposed budget allocation for this consultancy is approximately US$135,000. Services will be provided on a time and materials basis at an hourly or daily rate agreed before execution. The consultant will submit monthly invoices showing time worked and services provided, along with a brief progress report against the workplan. The Consultant manages their own schedule and working arrangements and is responsible for their own taxes, insurance, equipment, and benefits. Contract Oversight and Coordination GEM, as the current host of the ORA Consortium, will be the contracting party and administer the consultancy. GEM’s Chief Data Officer is the primary technical and contract contact, confirms milestones with the consultant, and approves deliverables against the agreed scope and acceptance criteria. This oversight concerns project requirements and outputs; the consultant remains responsible for how the services are performed. The Consultant will coordinate with the Chief Data Officer, GEM’s director of Product and the ORA Secretariat Coordinator to obtain member input, arrange reviews, and support delivery. The Secretariat Coordinator will review deliverables in partnership with the Chief Data Officer, and GEM will make payments under the terms of the contract. Minimum Qualifications and Preferred Qualifications: The successful candidate will be evaluated based on the following minimum and preferred qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: A minimum of 8 years of working experience in data architecture, data management, or data product development, preferably in climate and energy data. Demonstrated experience facilitating and managing technical projects or working groups across multiple organizations in English. Preferred Qualifications: Strong facilitation skills and experience building consensus among organizations with different practices and priorities. Demonstrated experience designing or implementing data integration and interoperability, such as common schemas, identifiers or entity resolution, metadata standards, and data documentation. Knowledge of the open energy data ecosystem, including open datasets, open-source energy modeling tools, and reproducible data pipelines. Experience with platform architecture choices (hosted, federated, and hybrid), versioned data releases, and APIs. Understanding of how AI systems consume data, including machine-readable metadata, APIs, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Experience working with open-source, open-data, digital public goods, research, or mission-driven organizations, including governance, licensing, and data stewardship. Based in Europe, to support time zone overlap with consortium members. Eligibility for an independent consultancy will be assessed in the country where the services will be performed before a contract is offered. Application Submission Details Interested candidates must submit their CV and cover letter through GEM’s Careers Page no later than November 11, 2026. Please provide: Resume or CV. Cover letter: a brief letter addressing (1) your experience related to the assignment - including past experience with data integration, interoperability standards, and facilitation across multiple organizations; (2) your availability and earliest start date; and (3) your location and time zone. One or two examples of relevant work, such as a data architecture proposal, interoperability framework, technical roadmap, or report developed through collaboration across organizations. Please briefly describe your contribution to each example. Links or anonymized excerpts are welcome; please do not submit confidential materials. Your proposed hourly or daily rate in US dollars. If quoting a daily rate, please indicate the number of hours included. References may be requested from shortlisted candidates. The evaluation committee will evaluate applications based on the preferred skills and experience outlined above and availability to undertake the assignment. GEM reserves the right to request clarification, conduct interviews with shortlisted candidates, negotiate the final scope and terms, or decline to make an award. Originally posted on Himalayas

Diagnose problems involving component selection, parasitics, layout, power integrity, signal integrity, thermal behavior, interfaces, or manufacturing. Review AI-generated circuit solutions and identify incorrect assumptions, invalid configurations, or unsupported conclusions. Develop reproducible reference solutions and automated verification checks. Required Skills Python Circuit Design Required Qualifications An MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline; or A BS in Electrical Engineering plus at least 1–2 years of relevant professional circuit-design experience. Practical proficiency with Python Experience with at least one EDA, circuit-simulation, PCB, HDL, synthesis, or verification tool that supports CLI, scripting, text-based inputs, or a programmatic API. Strong understanding of circuit behavior, component selection, tolerances, failure modes, and design trade-offs. description: Transactional Revenue Intelligence & Systems Analyst Location: LATAM · Work Model: Fully remote · Language: Spanish + English C1/C2 About Koronet Koronet is the leading vertical SaaS, B2B e-commerce, and payments software company for the over $50 Billion global B2B floral industry. Our solution consists of an inventory and operations management SaaS solution and an e-commerce network that enables end-to-end transactions through the B2B supply chain. Managing many of the largest businesses in the industry, our products help keep florists’ shelves stocked, weddings brightly bloomed, and Valentine’s Day brilliant red. Role Mission: Koronet grows when our customers succeed in buying, selling, and operating. Your job is to build the systems and intelligence that identify where we can add value, what blocks that growth, and how to scale our impact. You will work as a solo operator, not a passive analyst. You will build dashboards, decision-making tools that empower teams to act faster and smarter and execute scalable campaigns. You are responsible for transforming raw data into clear, actionable insights and driving real business outcomes at scale. How we work: We’re one team with one goal: delivering actual value. We share what we learn from customers, help our colleagues succeed, and focus on outcomes, not just checking boxes like 'completed call' or 'closed ticket.' Transactions at Koronet : Transactions connect how our customers actually work with what our platform can do. We sit between customer feedback and product development, turning what we see in the field into real product improvements. We don't just 'do tasks'—we look for ways to solve problems and use what we learn to make the whole platform better for everyone. What you will do: Build and maintain dashboards and tools for Transactions, Success, Product, and leadership. Connect data from calls, feedback, email, and market research to understand how customers buy, list, and sell. Drive the marketplace growth model by helping customers improve their sourcing, catalog reliability, and digital sales. Create feedback loops to track if campaigns and product changes actually drive adoption, transaction volume, or efficiency. Design, launch, and execute campaigns to expand and make buying and selling digitally in our ecosystem easier. Track impact on and ensure data quality by investigating inconsistencies rather than guessing. Turn customer insights into clear evidence for other teams to use. Identify and fix internal bottlenecks with automation and better workflows. How you will use tools: You will be a solo operator using automation, data analysis, and research tools to move faster. Define the problem, inputs, and goals clearly. Use research and prototyping to build better workflows. Measure results against real customer outcomes. Know when to use automation and when to rely on human judgment or customer context. Success Criteria: You drive business results at scale through your campaigns and indirectly enabling teams Customer-facing teams have stronger context to drive customer behavior. Product receives clear, prioritized evidence of customer problems and their impact. Insights compound over time into better enablement and product decisions. Your dashboards are trusted because they are accurate and useful, not because they are complex. You accelerate other teams without becoming a bottleneck. A few things this role isn't! A passive reporting or dashboard-making role. A product manager making roadmap promises. The final decision-maker on strategy. An AI developer hired only to build agents. What do we expect from you: Strong analytical judgment and commercial curiosity. Able to solve ambiguous problems using data, spreadsheets, SQL, or code. Comfortable working across structured and unstructured data. Excellent communication skills; you can turn complex data into useful narratives for other teams. Interest in marketplaces, B2B SaaS, and operational systems. Humble, rigorous, and team-first: you surface uncertainty and improve the system rather than defending your first guess.
